A blind solver can pick the key as the Pythagorean combination of two other options; 8.0 and 10.0 are the two single-axis legs (limiting-case distractors). Only 14.9 is a non-structural distractor.

AM16G-07.bounds: CT < BC = 10, kills none. Monotonicity: CA > AB so the tangent segment at C exceeds that at B, i.e. CT > BC/2 = 5 — kills 4 and 5 (5 sits ON the bound: equal-split/midpoint limiting case). Survivors 6 and 5.5.
AM16G-07.free_elimination: 5 is the midpoint (equilateral limiting case, §13b); 4 is BT (s - CA), the partner segment. Ordering CT > BT is a free intuition.

AM16G-09.free_elimination: Recall: pi/6 ~= 52.4% is a commonly memorised ratio; 66.7 is the sphere/cylinder 2/3 (Archimedes) recall confusion.

Incircle (95.2) < area < circumcircle (145.5) kills 152.2 but needs the apothem/circumradius trig (the work). Isoperimetric bound P^2/(4pi)=127.3 would kill 152.2, 136.1, 129.4 but is not ACT-level knowledge — not counted.
